description: Improve performance with Django's caching framework

slides.title: Introduction to Caching
slides.content:
# Django Caching 🚀

Speed up your site by storing computed results!

## What you'll learn:
- **Cache types** - Different caching backends
- **Using cache in views and templates** - Practical usage

## Why Cache?

```
Without Cache:
Request → Query DB → Process → Render → Response
                  (slow!)           

With Cache:
Request → Check Cache → HIT? Return cached → Response
                      → MISS? Generate & store → Response
```

## What to Cache?

- 📊 **Database queries** - Expensive queries
- 🖼️ **Rendered templates** - Complex pages
- 🔌 **API responses** - External API calls
- 📈 **Computed results** - Heavy calculations

## Performance Impact

| Scenario | Without Cache | With Cache |
|----------|--------------|------------|
| DB Query | 100ms | 1ms |
| Page Render | 500ms | 10ms |
| API Call | 2000ms | 5ms |

> 💡 **Caching is the fastest way to speed up Django!**

slides.title: Cache Types
Using Cache in Views
slides.content:
# Caching in Views 📝

## Low-Level Cache API

```python
from django.core.cache import cache

def get_products(request):
    # Try to get from cache
    products = cache.get('products_list')
    
    if products is None:
        # Cache miss - fetch from database
        products = list(Product.objects.all().values())
        # Store in cache for 5 minutes (300 seconds)
        cache.set('products_list', products, 300)
    
    return JsonResponse({'products': products})

# Other cache operations
cache.get('key', default='not found')  # Get with default
cache.set('key', 'value', timeout=60)  # Set with timeout
cache.delete('key')                     # Delete key
cache.clear()                           # Clear all
```

## View Caching Decorator

```python
from django.views.decorators.cache import cache_page

@cache_page(60 * 15)  # Cache for 15 minutes
def product_list(request):
    products = Product.objects.all()
    return render(request, 'products.html', {'products': products})
```

## Per-View Cache in URLs

```python
from django.views.decorators.cache import cache_page

urlpatterns = [
    path('products/', cache_page(60 * 15)(views.product_list)),
]
```

## Conditional Caching

```python
def product_detail(request, pk):
    cache_key = f'product_{pk}'
    product = cache.get(cache_key)
    
    if product is None:
        product = get_object_or_404(Product, pk=pk)
        cache.set(cache_key, product, 3600)  # 1 hour
    
    return render(request, 'detail.html', {'product': product})
```

slides.title: Using Cache in Templates
slides.content:
# Template Fragment Caching 🧩 Cache parts of templates! ## Fragment Caching ```html {% load cache %} {% cache 500 sidebar %}
{% for item in expensive_query %}

{{ item.name }}

{% endfor %}
{% endcache %} {% cache 300 user_sidebar request.user.id %}
Welcome, {{ request.user.username }}!
{% endcache %} ``` ## Cache Invalidation ```python from django.core.cache import cache # When product is updated, invalidate cache def update_product(request, pk): product = Product.objects.get(pk=pk) # ... update product ... product.save() # Invalidate related caches cache.delete(f'product_{pk}') cache.delete('products_list') ``` ## Cache Versioning ```python # Increment version to invalidate all keys CACHES = { 'default': { 'BACKEND': '...', 'VERSION': 2, # Change to invalidate all } } ``` > 💡 **Cache invalidation is hard!** Always have a strategy for clearing stale data.

slides.title: Summary
slides.content:
# Excellent Work! 🎉

You've mastered Django Caching!

## Cache Types
- ✅ **Local Memory** - Development
- ✅ **Redis** - Production (recommended)
- ✅ **Memcached** - High performance
- ✅ **Database** - Simple persistence
- ✅ **File-based** - Shared filesystem

## Using Cache in Views
- ✅ `cache.get()` / `cache.set()`
- ✅ `@cache_page(seconds)` decorator
- ✅ `cache.delete()` for invalidation

## Using Cache in Templates
- ✅ `{% load cache %}`
- ✅ `{% cache timeout name %}` tag
- ✅ Variable cache keys for per-user caching

## Cache API Summary

```python
from django.core.cache import cache

cache.set('key', value, timeout)  # Store
cache.get('key', default=None)    # Retrieve
cache.delete('key')               # Remove
cache.clear()                     # Clear all
```

## Best Practices
- 💡 Use Redis for production
- 💡 Set appropriate timeouts
- 💡 Invalidate on data changes
- 💡 Use meaningful cache keys

> 🎉 **Congratulations!** You've completed Django Caching!
